title: The projection-formula morphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Work on small representatives of the small etale sites in a universe large enough for the module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], and use the unbounded module derived categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The constant-coefficient module inverse image $f^{-1}$ is the exact left adjoint to $f_*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. On derived categories $f^{-1}$ is its termwise derived functor [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. For a representing complex $C$ choose a K-injective resolution $C\to I$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and let $Rf_*(QC)=Q(f_*I)$ be the total right derived functor [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Use the canonical derived adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*$, with unit $\eta_f$ and counit $\varepsilon_f$: its Hom bijection is the termwise adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] computed on a K-injective resolution of the second argument, using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective].

All tensor products are the ordinary uncompleted derived tensor products of [def-kun-derived-tensor], acting on morphisms by the derived tensor bifunctor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Put $M=Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}K$ and $N=E\kunotimes{\Lambda}f^{-1}K$. Let
$$
 c_{Rf_*E,K}:f^{-1}(Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}K)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}f^{-1}Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}f^{-1}K
$$
be the inverse of the canonical comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], and put
$$
 \alpha_{E,K}=(\varepsilon_{f,E}\kunotimes{\Lambda}1_{f^{-1}K})\circ c_{Rf_*E,K}:f^{-1}M\longrightarrow N.
$$
The *projection-formula morphism* is the explicit composite in $D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$
$$
 \mathrm{PF}_f(E,K):\quad
 Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}K=M
 \xrightarrow{\eta_{f,M}}Rf_*f^{-1}M
 \xrightarrow{Rf_*(\alpha_{E,K})}Rf_*N
 =Rf_*(E\kunotimes{\Lambda}f^{-1}K).
$$
Equivalently it is the morphism adjoint to $\alpha_{E,K}$ under the displayed derived adjunction. No boundedness, properness, finiteness or torsion condition is imposed, and no assertion that this morphism is invertible is part of the definition.

    derivedTensorRightDerivedLowerStar A p ⟶
      rightDerivedLowerStarDerivedTensorLeftDerivedUpperStar A p
lean.note: Specialize A to ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ, with Λ : Type (u + 1), [CommRing Λ], and p to f : X ⟶ Y of Scheme.{u}; evaluate the natural transformation at E,K. Import WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.UpperLowerStar.FlatModuleCat for upperStarPreservesFlat_moduleCat. ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution and the standard module-category instances discharge all coefficient hypotheses, with no boundedness, properness, finiteness or torsion hypothesis. The categories are exactly DerivedCategoryModule Λ X/Y of def-weil-pbc-derived-categories. leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory identifies the left derived pullback with the exact termwise inverse image; derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction is induced from the termwise adjunction and the K-injective right-derived comparison. The tensor comparison is leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison, the hom of leftDerivedUpperStarTensorNatIso, hence the inverse of the comparison in the direction displayed in lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal. rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap_app_app is the adjunction mate of this comparison followed by tensoring the counit with the identity. Mathlib Adjunction.homEquiv_unit gives exactly η_M followed by Rf_*(α). The transpose equation is homEquiv_symm_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap. The specialization compiles via scompile.py and #print axioms of the existing definition lists only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No duplicate definition or extra theorem is introduced.
